question:
Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) has successfully completed the ground test of the solid fuel-based booster stage (SS1) of its new SSLV at Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota at Andhra Pradesh in March 2022. 

What is the full form of the above mentioned SSLV?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Small Satellite Launch Vehicle.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Small Satellite Launch Vehicle**

 
 
• **​ISRO** developed the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV), a small-lift launch vehicle that can support multiple orbital drop-offs and can deliver **payloads of 500 kg** (1,100 Lb) to **low Earth orbit **(500 km (310 mi)) or 300 kg (660 lb) to **Sun-synchronous orbit **(500 km (310 mi) for the launch of small satellites.
 
• With launch-on-demand **flexibility and minimal infrastructure **requirements, SSLV is developed with low cost and quick turnaround in mind.
 
• The SSLV was developed with the intention of commercially launching small satellites at a significantly** lower cost** and with a** higher launch rate** than the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV).**
 
• While a small team of about six people would oversee SSLV launch operations, a PSLV launch involves **600 officials.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Systematic Satellite Launch Vehicle**

 
 
• **​**The Indian Space Research Organization started the small The SLV was designed to carry a **payload of 40 kg (88 lb)** and **travel 400 kilometres (250 miles) in height.** In **August 1979**, SLV-3's first experimental **flight was a failure**. On **July 18, 1980**, the **first successful launch** took place.
 
 
 
• **Synchronized Satellite Launch Vehicle**
 
 
• **​**The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) designed, developed, and operates the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV), an expendable space launch vehicle for launching satellites and other space objects into geosynchronous transfer orbits. **GSLV stands 49.13 meters tall**, making it the tallest **ISRO vehicle.**
 
• It is a vehicle with three stages and a lift-off mass of** 420 Tonnes**.
 
 
 
• **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle**
 
 
• **​**The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) created and operates the reusable **medium-lift launch **vehicle known as the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV).
 
• It was designed to make it possible for India to launch its** Indian Remote Sensing (IRS)** satellites into sun-synchronous orbits, a service that was only commercially available from Russia prior to the PSLV's introduction in 1993.
 
• Additionally, PSLV is capable of sending small satellites into Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO).
